conversation.content:
Good morning, and welcome to our session today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you've taken this time for yourself, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As we navigate the journey of motherhood together, I want to ensure that you feel comfortable and supported throughout our conversation.

Today, we'll be using the EPDS, which is a tool designed to help us understand how you're feeling during this postpartum period. The purpose of this assessment is to check in with you about your emotional well-being and identify any areas where you might need some extra support. Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and a safe space for you to express yourself honestly.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better understanding of your feelings and experiences over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. This will help me get a sense of how you're doing and what might be helpful for you right now.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this is a judgment-free zone. I'm here to listen, support, and provide guidance, not to criticize or diagnose. My goal is to create a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself freely.

So, let's get started. The first question is: Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself, and have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do?

.. to be honest, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. Taking care of the baby is exhausting, and some days I just feel like I'm going through the motions. I used to love reading and taking long walks, but lately, I just haven't had the energy or interest in doing those things. I mean, I'll pick up a book, but I'll only read a few pages before I fall asleep or get distracted by the baby's needs. And walks? Forget about it, I'm lucky if I get out of the house with a shower some days. 

As for enjoying things, it's just not the same. I feel like I've lost my sense of purpose, and everything feels so much harder now. Even simple tasks, like laundry or cooking, just seem like too much effort. I've been feeling really sad and discouraged, and some days I just feel like I'm not doing enough or that I'm not a good enough mom. It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just going through the motions, trying to keep everything together, but inside, I'm feeling really empty and unsure of myself. 

I guess what I'm trying to say is that I just don't feel like myself anymore. I feel like I've lost my identity, and I'm just trying to figure out who I am now as a mom. It's scary, and it's hard, and some days I just feel like I'm barely holding on. Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

To be honest, I haven't been laughing as much as I used to. I mean, I'll catch myself smiling when my baby does something cute, but it's not the same as really laughing and feeling carefree. Most of the time, I'm just too tired or preoccupied with worries about the baby's health and safety to really enjoy things. I'll be in the middle of a task, and suddenly I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and it just feels like this weight is crushing me. 

I do try to put on a happy face for my baby, though. I want her to be happy and healthy, and I know that my mood can affect hers. But when I'm alone, or when my partner is taking care of the baby, I often find myself crying or just feeling really down. It's like I'm just going through the motions, trying to be a good mom, but inside, I'm struggling to find the joy in things. 

Sometimes, I'll be talking to my partner or a friend, and they'll say something funny, and I'll laugh, but it's not the same as it used to be. It's like I'm laughing on the outside, but inside, I'm still feeling really sad and anxious. I miss feeling like myself, you know? I miss being able to laugh and enjoy things without all this weight on my shoulders.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

.. I don't really look forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll plan something, like a walk with my baby or a visit with friends, but then the day of, I'll just feel so overwhelmed and anxious that I'll end up canceling or just going through the motions. I'll think about all the things that could go wrong, like the baby crying or me forgetting something important, and it just feels like too much. 

Even things that I used to enjoy, like taking a bath or reading a book, just don't bring me the same joy as they used to. I'll think about doing something relaxing, but then I'll start worrying about the baby's schedule or whether I'm doing everything right, and it just feels like there's no point. 

Sometimes, my partner will suggest doing something fun, like going out for dinner or seeing a movie, and I'll just feel like it's too much effort. I'll think about all the things I need to do to get ready, and the baby's needs, and it just feels overwhelming. I'll say yes, but then I'll just feel anxious and stressed, thinking about all the things that could go wrong. 

I miss looking forward to things, you know? I miss feeling excited and happy about plans or activities. Now, everything just feels like a chore or a source of stress. I guess that's just part of being a new mom, but it's hard not to feel like I've lost myself in all of this.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot. I mean, if the baby cries, I immediately think it's because I'm not doing something right. If she's not sleeping well, I think it's because I didn't establish a good routine. If she's not eating well, I think it's because I'm not making enough milk or that I'm not feeding her correctly. It's like, no matter what happens, I always seem to find a way to blame myself. 

And it's not just with the baby. If I'm feeling tired or overwhelmed, I'll think it's because I'm not managing my time well or that I'm not prioritizing things correctly. I'll think that if I were a better mom, I'd be able to handle all of this without feeling so exhausted and stressed. 

I know it's not rational, but it's hard to shake off the feeling that I'm just not doing enough or that I'm not good enough. I'll be scrolling through social media, and I'll see all these other moms who seem to have it together, and I'll think, "Why can't I be like that?" It's like, I'm constantly comparing myself to others and coming up short. 

My partner tries to tell me that I'm doing a great job, that I'm an amazing mom, but it's hard to hear that when I'm feeling so guilty and inadequate all the time. I just wish I could be kinder to myself, you know? I wish I could just say, "Okay, mistakes happen, and it's okay," but it's hard to let go of that self-blame. It's like, it's just always there, lurking in the back of my mind, making me feel like I'm not good enough.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... I've been feeling really anxious and worried a lot lately. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if she chokes on something? What if she gets sick? What if I'm not doing enough to protect her? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I feel like I'm on edge all the time. 

And it's not just about the baby. I'll worry about my relationship with my partner, or about how I'm managing the household, or about whether I'm doing enough to take care of myself. It's like, I'll find something to worry about, no matter what. And even when my partner or friends try to reassure me, I just can't shake off the feeling of anxiety. 

Sometimes, I'll be in the middle of a task, and I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like, my body is reacting to this perceived threat, even though there's no real reason to be scared. It's so frustrating, because I know it's not rational, but I just can't seem to calm myself down. 

I've been having trouble sleeping, too, because my mind just won't shut off. I'll lie there, thinking about all the things I need to do, or worrying about the baby, or just feeling anxious about everything. It's like, I'm stuck in this cycle of worry and fear, and I don't know how to get out of it. 

It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'm constantly on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And even when nothing does go wrong, I still feel like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop. It's exhausting, and it's making it hard for me to enjoy this time with my baby, which is supposed to be so special.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... I've been feeling really scared and panicky a lot lately. It's like, my heart will start racing and I'll feel this overwhelming sense of fear, but when I try to think about what's causing it, there's no real reason. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or playing with her, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. It's like, my body is reacting to something, but my mind can't catch up with what it is.

Sometimes, it's triggered by little things, like a strange noise or a sudden movement. But other times, it just seems to come out of nowhere. I'll be feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll be hit with this feeling of dread or fear. It's like, my mind is playing tricks on me, making me think that something is wrong when everything is actually okay.

It's really scary, because I feel like I'm losing control. I'll be in the middle of a task, and I'll just feel like I'm going to pass out or something. My partner will try to calm me down, but it's hard to explain what's happening. I'll just feel like I'm frozen in fear, like I'm stuck in this moment and can't move forward.

I've been having trouble leaving the house, too, because I'm scared of what might happen. I'll think about all the things that could go wrong, like the baby getting hurt or me getting into an accident. It's like, my mind is just filled with all these worst-case scenarios, and I don't know how to make them stop.

It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'm living in a state of constant hypervigilance. I'm always on the lookout for potential dangers, always waiting for something to go wrong. And even when nothing does go wrong, I still feel like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop. It's exhausting, and it's making it hard for me to enjoy this time with my baby.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... things have been feeling really overwhelming lately. I mean, taking care of a new baby is a lot of work, and it's like, I'm just trying to keep my head above water most of the time. The lack of sleep doesn't help, either. I'm just so tired all the time, and it's hard to think clearly or make decisions when I'm running on fumes.

And it's not just the baby, it's everything else too. The laundry, the dishes, the cooking... it's like, I'm just trying to keep up with all of these responsibilities, but I feel like I'm falling behind. My partner tries to help, but it's hard to delegate tasks when I feel like I'm the only one who can do things right.

Sometimes, I'll be in the middle of doing something, and I'll just feel like I'm in way over my head. I'll think, "How am I going to get everything done? How am I going to take care of the baby and keep the house clean and cook meals?" It's like, my mind is just racing with all of these tasks and responsibilities, and I feel like I'm just going to collapse under the weight of it all.

I've been feeling really emotional, too. I'll be doing something, and then I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm just so overwhelmed and stressed, and I don't know how to make it stop. My partner will try to comfort me, but it's hard to explain what's going on. I just feel like I'm drowning in all of these responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.

It's hard, because I feel like I should be able to handle all of this. I mean, I'm a mom now, and I'm supposed to be capable and competent. But the truth is, I'm just struggling to keep up. And it's hard to admit that, because I feel like I'm failing somehow. But I guess that's just the reality of being a new mom, right?
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... I've been having a really hard time sleeping lately. I mean, it's not just the baby waking me up all the time, it's like, my mind is just racing and I couldn't relax even if I wanted to. I'll lie in bed and just think about all the things that are worrying me, like the baby's health, or my relationship with my partner, or just feeling like I'm not doing a good job as a mom.

And even when I do fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are just so unsettling. I'll dream that something is wrong with the baby, or that I'm in danger, or just something that's really disturbing. And then I'll wake up feeling anxious and on edge, and it's hard to shake that feeling off.

I've been having trouble falling asleep, too. I'll lie in bed for hours, just staring at the ceiling and thinking about all the things that are bothering me. My partner will try to reassure me, but it's hard to calm my mind down when I'm feeling so overwhelmed. And then, when the baby wakes up, I'll be exhausted, but I'll still have to get up and take care of her.

It's like, I'm just caught in this cycle of stress and anxiety, and I don't know how to get out of it. I'll try to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to put into words. I just feel like I'm failing, like I'm not doing enough, and that's just really hard to deal with.

Sometimes, I'll cry myself to sleep, just feeling so overwhelmed and unhappy. It's like, I'm just not the person I used to be, and I don't know how to get back to that place. I miss feeling happy and carefree, but it's like, that's just not an option for me right now. And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my baby, but the truth is, I'm just really struggling.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... I've been feeling really sad and miserable a lot lately. It's like, this constant cloud of sadness is just following me around, and I don't know how to shake it off. I'll be doing things with the baby, like feeding her or playing with her, and I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm happy to be with her, but at the same time, I'm just so overwhelmed and sad.

I feel like I've lost myself, like I'm just a mom now and not a person. I miss the things I used to enjoy, like reading or going for walks, but now it's just too hard to find the time or energy. And even when I do get some time to myself, I just feel guilty for not spending it with the baby.

I've been feeling really discouraged, too. Like, I'll try to do something, and it won't work out, and I'll just feel like I've failed. Or I'll look at other moms, and they'll seem so put together and happy, and I'll just feel like I'm not measuring up. It's like, I'm constantly comparing myself to others, and I'm always coming up short.

Sometimes, I'll just feel like I'm not good enough, like I'm not doing enough for the baby or for my partner. And that feeling is just so crushing, it's like, it's hard to breathe. I'll try to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to put into words. I just feel like I'm drowning in this sea of sadness and self-doubt.

I've been having thoughts of "what's the point?" or "I'm not doing a good job," and it's hard to shake those thoughts off. It's like, I'm just trapped in this cycle of sadness and negativity, and I don't know how to escape. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really living. And that's a really hard thing to admit, because I feel like I should be happy and grateful for this little life I've been given. But the truth is, I'm just really struggling.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be doing something, and suddenly I'll just start sobbing. It's not even always about anything in particular, it's just like, this overwhelming feeling of sadness and frustration will just wash over me, and I'll start crying.

I've been crying a lot when I'm alone, but also when I'm with my partner or friends. It's like, I'll try to hold it together, but then something will just trigger me, and I'll start crying. It's really embarrassing, because I feel like I'm losing control, and I don't know how to stop it.

Sometimes, I'll cry because I'm just so tired and overwhelmed. I'll be taking care of the baby, and I'll just feel like I'm at my breaking point, and I'll start crying. Other times, I'll cry because I'm feeling so guilty or inadequate. I'll think about all the things I'm not doing right, or all the things I'm not giving the baby, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness and regret, and I'll start crying.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be strong and capable, but the truth is, I'm just really struggling. I'm struggling to take care of the baby, to take care of myself, to keep my relationship with my partner healthy... it's just all so much, and sometimes it feels like too much to bear.

I've been trying to hide my tears from my partner, but it's hard. They'll see me crying, and they'll try to comfort me, but it's hard to explain what's going on. I just feel like I'm a mess, like I'm not the person I used to be, and I don't know how to get back to that place. I just feel like I'm lost, and I don't know how to find my way again.
